summary: A ROS Answers forum thread (question 310626, asked 2018-12-13 by user poonam1120) about how to express a dictionary-style filter configuration in ROS 2 YAML, specifically a TransferFunction block with filter coefficients a and b. Commenter tfoote replied that YAML syntax has not changed and that the snippet resembles an old nodelet config replaced by components. The accepted-style answer posted 2018-12-20 provides a working LowPass example using the MultiChannelTransferFunctionFilter<double> type with name transferfunction_test, showing the params layout is unchanged.
one_line: ROS Answers thread on writing a nodelet-style transfer function filter dictionary in ROS 2 YAML, with a working LowPass example.
key_facts: The ROS Answers question 310626 'Dictionary item in yaml in ros2' was asked on 2018-12-13 13:09:07 -0500 by user poonam1120.
The original question tagged ros2 and bouncy sought to convert a TransferFunction YAML block into ROS 2 YAML.
The original TransferFunction block used type filters/MultiChannelTransferFunctionFilterDouble with params a: [1.0, -1.760041880343169, 1.182893262037831].
The original TransferFunction block's params also included b: [0.018098933007514, 0.054296799022543, 0.054296799022543, 0.018098933007514].
User tfoote commented on 2018-12-14 that YAML syntax has not changed in ROS 2.
tfoote stated the snippet looks like a nodelet YAML config, which has been replaced by the concept of components.
The answer was posted 2018-12-20 12:48:18 -0500 by poonam1120, who said the code was working and that the params declaration had not changed.
The working answer uses a LowPass block with name transferfunction_test and type MultiChannelTransferFunctionFilter<double>.
The question had 939 views and was last updated Dec 20 '18.
ROS Answers announced as deprecated as of August 11, 2023, in favor of robotics.stackexchange.com.
